resources.string: Battery saver or full speed, CPU speed limit and overclock
Longer play time. The CPU stays at or below %1$s and the graphics at %2$d MHz. Plenty for 8 and 16-bit games.
Standard speeds. The processor speeds up when a game needs it and slows down when it doesn\'t.
Smoothest emulation. The CPU never drops below %1$s, the graphics run at %2$d MHz and the memory at full speed all the time. For PS1, N64 and PSP games. The battery runs down faster.
\n\nThe profile is kept when the console restarts. The Quick Settings tile switches to the next one.
\n\nThe profile is kept when the console restarts. FN + R1 and the Quick Settings tile switch to the next one.
Close background apps when opening any game
Frees memory for the game, the same as Close background apps in the power menu
Lower means longer battery life and a cooler console, but slower games. If a game slows down, pick a higher speed. Kept when the console restarts.
%1$s. The profile keeps the CPU at %2$s or lower right now.
%1$s. On hold while the overclock is on.
Off, the CPU runs at up to %1$s

Faster emulation for demanding games, at a cost: the console gets warmer, the battery drains faster, and some consoles freeze or crash at the higher speeds. If that happens, pick a lower speed.\n\nThe console always starts without the overclock, a restart turns it off. While it is on, the maximum CPU speed is on hold. The console also slows down by itself when it gets too hot.

Runs the CPU at a slightly lower voltage for the same speed, so it uses a bit less power and stays a bit cooler, mostly at the higher speeds. At 816 MHz and below there is little to gain.

Every chip is different. If a game crashes or the console freezes or restarts, go back to Off. A crash while something is being saved can damage files on the card, so go one step at a time and play for a while before going lower.

The console always starts with the undervolt off, a restart turns it off.
Off: up to %2$s, %1$s with the overclock

This speed runs the GPU and memory power line at its highest voltage. Some memory chips handle it, others make games crash, freeze the console or mess up the picture.
It can\'t damage the memory, but a crash while something is being saved can damage files on the card. If anything acts up, go back to a lower speed. A restart turns it off.

Faster graphics and memory for demanding games. The GPU overclock runs the GPU at 600 MHz instead of 520 MHz. The faster memory speeds help emulators like PPSSPP the most. Both raise the voltage of the power line the GPU and memory share, so the console gets a bit warmer and the battery drains a bit faster.
Every chip is different. If a game crashes or the console freezes, turn them off. The console always starts without them, a restart turns them off.
Based on R36 Tuner Next by zenmode-adri.
This console\'s system doesn\'t have this speed
Couldn\'t change the GPU or memory speed

plurals.name: app_profiles_on
plurals.item: On, %d app has its own profile
On, %d apps have their own profile

resources.string: An app with its own profile gets it while it is open. The profile chosen in Performance comes back when you leave the app.

Default means the app follows the profile chosen in Performance. Some emulators start out with Performance and some apps with Balanced or Battery saver. Change any of them here.

The Quick Settings tile and FN + R1 still work in an app that has its own profile. Your pick then lasts until you leave the app.

While this is on, a small helper watches which app is open. It doesn't run while this is off or no app has its own profile.
